summary: A multi-line text field with label, description and error built in, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label and accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps external <label for> from reaching the inner textarea.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name.

errorMessage.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid.

value.note: Current text; submitted with the form.

placeholder.note: Example of the expected input. Never a substitute for the label.

autocomplete.note: Native autocomplete token (WCAG 1.3.5 for personal data).

required.note: Native required, plus an aria-hidden asterisk after the label . Explain * once per form.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Vertical stack with the field gap.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: textarea
anatomy.notes: Native <textarea>; receives focus, typing and validation. Min height 64px, resizes vertically.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each edit. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Value committed (blur). Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed. Enter inserts a newline and never changes the commit state.

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring and border in ring color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

error.trigger: error-message set, or native validity fails after blur or a submit attempt

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals: setFormValue on the textarea value, validity mirrored with setValidity (anchored to the inner textarea), formResetCallback restores the default value, disabled fields are not submitted.

accessibility.focusRingVisible: On focus of the textarea; 3px ring in textarea.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Enter: inserts a newline; it never submits the owning form (native textarea behavior)

aria: aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required on the input; the asterisk is aria-hidden
errorMessage: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
aria-invalid="true" on the host marks the inner textarea invalid too (as errorMessage does), so a wrapper such as sb-input-group can mark it
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region; fix over the reference implementation, where the error is only read on focus)

useCases.when: Longer free text: comments, messages, descriptions, notes
The label would repeat visible context
Limits or format need explaining before typing

useCases.use: errorMessage with what went wrong and how to fix it

antiPatterns.pattern: Textarea for a short single-line value
antiPatterns.why: Wastes space and hides the expected length
It disappears on typing and is not a reliable accessible name
Enter inserts a newline in a textarea

coverage: label is the name; label click focuses; min height 64px; vertical resize
description and error in the accessible description; aria-invalid
native validity after blur, not on first typing
input on edit, change on commit, both composed
Enter inserts a newline, never submits
form value, validity, minlength, reset, disabled, disabled fieldset, errorMessage customError, label for

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Textarea
drift.realization: shadcn composes Field parts around Textarea; shadow DOM requires them inside
shadcn default border-input is neutral-200; changed for WCAG 1.4.11
shadcn uses field-sizing-content (auto-grow); brief asks for vertical resize

coverage: Textarea: 6 variant(s), State (Rest, Focus) x Validation (None, Error) x Disabled (False, True); read back ok

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: modeled on Input; native textarea semantics.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter submit the form?
openQuestions.answer: No. Native textarea inserts a newline; no implicit submission.

openQuestions.question: Auto-grow?
openQuestions.answer: No. Min height 64px with vertical resize.
